title: Deep learning foundations
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Understand and build neural networks from the ground up: neurons and multilayer perceptrons, loss functions, backpropagation as reverse-mode automatic differentiation (by writing a tiny autograd engine), training loops, initialization, optimizers in practice, regularization with weight decay, dropout and early stopping, normalization layers, training diagnostics, residual connections, and how frameworks such as PyTorch organize the same ideas.
primary_reading: Understanding Deep Learning by Simon Prince (free PDF)

weeks.1: Neurons, activation functions and the multilayer perceptron
weeks.2: Loss functions: squared error and cross-entropy
weeks.3: Computational graphs and the chain rule
weeks.5: Training a network: mini-batches, epochs and learning rates
weeks.7: Optimizers in practice: momentum and Adam
weeks.8: Regularization: weight decay, dropout and early stopping
weeks.9: Normalization: batch normalization and layer normalization
weeks.10: Training diagnostics: learning curves, vanishing and exploding gradients
weeks.11: Residual connections and very deep networks
weeks.12: Deep learning frameworks: tensors, modules and automatic differentiation

blocks.deliverable: Compute a forward pass and the loss of a small network by hand.
Build a scalar autograd engine and check it against finite differences.
Train a small network on a toy classification task from scratch.
Week 7 midterm; compare training with and without regularization.
Diagnose three failed training runs from their learning curves.
Describe how your from-scratch network maps onto a framework.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Neural network from scratch: extend your autograd engine into a small neural network library (layers, losses, an optimizer and a training loop), train a multilayer perceptron on a supplied classification data set, run an ablation of initialization, learning rate and regularization, and write a report with learning curves as tables and what each experiment shows.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
